Following our procurement checklist, DataMed is ready to move forward with Redwood for evaluation. Before we can execute a DPA we need:

- Current SOC 2 Type II report (or summary) and date range
- A recent penetration test summary and remediation status

Matt —

Thanks for the clear checklist. DocuSign is fine for us. I've looped in Neha (legal) and Vivek (security) to confirm evidence and subprocessors. Quick answers up front:

- SOC 2: we can provide a Type II summary now and an attestation letter; full report can be shared under NDA if required.
- Pen test: summary + remediation timeline available (we’ll attach).
- Subprocessors: we maintain a living list; will share current roster and a process for notifying changes.

Neha — can you draft a short response on acceptable DPA redline positions (audit scope, notice windows)? Vivek — can you attach the SOC 2 summary and pen test summary for Matt?

Subject: DPA redlines (initial) and proposed carve-outs

Hi Matt / team —

Please find our marked-up DPA attached. High-level summary of our positions:

1) Audit rights: we accept customer audits for cause with a 30-day notice period; remote-first is our standard. For on-site audits we require scope pre-approval and a mutually agreed schedule to avoid operational disruption.

2) Subprocessors: we will provide a current roster and commit to 30 days' notice of material changes; we cannot pre-approve every SaaS vendor but will give an option for review for sensitive categories.

3) Cross-border data transfers: SCCs will be executed where applicable; we will sign a Swiss addendum if required.

4) Data retention & logs: we prefer to keep retention limits aligned to the agreement; we can provide audit logs for a defined retention window (typically 90 days) and discuss extended retention for a commercial fee.

Attached: DPA_Redline_v2.docx (track changes).

If DataMed has specific clauses you'd like us to consider, send them over and we'll comment.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com
From: Tara Singh <tara.singh@datamed.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood-inference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: Matt Lee <procurement@datamed.com>
Date: 2026-11-26T11:03:00Z
Subject: RE: DPA redlines (initial) and proposed carve-outs

Thanks Neha — overall that helps. A few counterpoints from DataMed legal:

- Audit rights: DataMed needs an explicit on-site audit right in the DPA for our regulated customers (healthcare), with a 45-day notice window and an option to escalate if remote evidence is insufficient.
- Logs retention: we need at least 180 days of access to audit logs for compliance; please confirm any commercial terms for extended retention.
- Subprocessors: we will provide a narrow list of categories that require prior approval (e.g., cloud hosting, analytics).

Attached are our redlines for quick review: DataMed_DPA_redlines.docx. Can we schedule a call with your security team to walk through the pen-test findings and remediation?

Regards,
Tara Singh
Senior Counsel, DataMed Inc
